sentences.text: Yash Rai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025

Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:50579
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Jabalpur
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Devnarayan Mishra

On The 7 th Of October, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 34672 of 2025
 Yash Rai
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others

Appearance:
 Shri Satyam Agrawal - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Shivendra Shukla - Advocate for the objector.
 Shri Akshay Namdeo - Government Advocate for the resp
 State.

Order 
This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 o f Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita , 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.159/2024 registered at Police Station-Sendari, District-Tikamgarh (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 450,
376, 376D, 506 of IPC and Section 66E of IT Act.
The applicant is in custody since 18.05.2024.

Earlier bail application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 18.09.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.29990 of 2024.
2.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the victim has been examined.
From the deposition of the victim, it is clear that the applicant was involved in the first incident which has taken place on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50579 2 MCRC-34672-2025 26.04.2024.
From her statement, it is clear that the applicant has neither stated anything to the victim nor taken the photographs of the victim.
This applicant has also not made viral the objectionable photographs of the victim.
No FIR was lodged of the first incident and the FIR was lodged when the objectionable photographs of the victim got viral.
The applicant has falsely been implicated in the case and he is in custody since 18.05.2024, hence, he be released on bail.
3. Learned counsel for the objector has submitted that the applicant's active participation in the offence is proved, hence, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

4. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and submitted that DNA report is negative but till today four to five prosecution witnesses have been examined, hence, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

sentences.text: 5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6. Looking to the contents of FIR and examination of the victim, this Court deems it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on bail.
Thus, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of trial.

8. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50579 3 MCRC-34672-2025 provisions of Section 480 (3) of BNSS.
9.

Accordingly, M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
C.C. as per rules.
(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE HK Yash Rai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7961347/
